name: Aeneas
source_summary: A paralyzed man at Lydda, bedridden for eight years, healed instantly by the apostle Peter in Jesus' name -- a miracle that led the whole region of Lydda and Sharon to turn to the Lord.
family_friendly_summary: Aeneas was a man who lived in the town of Lydda. He had been paralyzed and stuck in bed for eight whole years. When the apostle Peter came to visit the believers in Lydda, he found Aeneas and said, "Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you; get up and make your bed!" Right away, Aeneas stood up completely healed. Everyone who lived in Lydda and the area around it heard about what happened, and many of them turned to believe in the Lord because of this amazing miracle.
adult_story: Aeneas was a man in Lydda who had been paralyzed and confined to his bed for eight years (Acts 9:33). As Peter traveled among the young churches during "a season of peace" for believers throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria (9:31), he came to Lydda and found Aeneas. Peter's words were direct and Christ-centered: "Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you; get up and make your bed" (9:34) -- Peter was careful to credit the healing to Jesus, not to himself. Aeneas got up immediately, fully restored after nearly a decade of paralysis. The effect rippled outward: "all who lived at Lydda and Sharon saw him, and they turned to the Lord" (9:35). Aeneas's healing is one of several miracles in Acts (alongside Tabitha's resurrection in the same chapter) that confirmed the apostles' preaching with the same kind of power Jesus Himself had shown, and drew a whole region to faith -- evidence that the risen Christ was still actively at work through His apostles after His ascension.
christ_connections: Lord Jesus, Peter made sure Aeneas knew it was You who healed him, not Peter. Every good thing I receive traces back to You the same way.
Eight years flat on a mat, and one word from You was enough to raise him up. I bring You my own long-stuck places and trust the same power is still Yours to give.
